questions.question: What is the composition of the MXene built from M = Cr, X = C, n = 1, passivation F?
Hands-on: mxene_formula('Mo,Ti', 'C', 2, 'O') = ?
questions.explanation: Ordered double-M: outer Mo layers, inner Ti.

questions.question: What is the 'fcc' termination site?

options.a: on top of the outer metal
options.b: the hollow above the metal of the opposite side (not above X)

questions.explanation: 'Model I'; hcp = above the X atom ('model II').

questions.question: Hands-on: Cr2CF2 — hcp minus fcc termination energy (meV/atom, integer)?
questions.explanation: ≈ +105 meV/atom: F prefers the fcc hollow.

questions.question: Hands-on: relaxed lattice constant a of Cr2CF2 (Å, 2 decimals)?
questions.explanation: 2.955 Å (CHGNet).

questions.question: Hands-on: E_hull of Cr2CF2 (meV/atom, integer)?
questions.explanation: 265 meV/atom above the Cr–C–F hull.

questions.question: Hands-on: into which bulk phases does Cr2CF2 decompose?
questions.explanation: 0.29 Cr7C3 + 0.11 C + 0.60 CrF2 (per atom).

questions.question: Hands-on: E_hull of Ni2NF2 (meV/atom, integer)?
questions.explanation: 377 meV/atom → Ni3N + N2 + NiF2.

questions.question: Hands-on: E_hull of bare 2D Mo2C (meV/atom, integer)?
questions.explanation: 391 meV/atom above bulk β-Mo2C — the cost of two bare surfaces.

questions.question: Why are all three monolayers above the hull?

options.b: 2D sheets have surface (unsaturated / terminated) bonds relative to the bulk competing phases — MXenes are metastable, made by etching

questions.explanation: Typical MXene E_hull values are a few hundred meV/atom.

questions.question: Hands-on: Δμ*_F for Cr2C → Cr2CF2 (eV, 2 decimals)?
questions.explanation: F termination is favoured for Δμ_F > −3.90 eV.

questions.question: What does Δμ_F > Δμ*_F mean?

options.b: fluorination of the bare sheet lowers the free energy (F-terminated surface wins)

questions.explanation: ΔG_F(Δμ) = [E(T) − E(bare) − 2μ⁰ − 2Δμ]/A < 0.

questions.question: Hands-on: CHGNet formation energy of CrF2 (eV/atom, 2 decimals)?
questions.explanation: −2.75 eV/atom vs experiment −2.69 eV/atom.

questions.question: Which energy model does the module use by default, and why?

options.b: CHGNet universal potential — Materials Project scale, works offline; screening quality

questions.explanation: Materials Project / OQMD may be unreachable; replace by VASP for publication.

questions.question: How do you replace the model energies by your own VASP results?

options.b: --energies CSV (formula or name, eV/atom), or write_vasp + symphase hull

questions.explanation: Both MXene and competing phases can be replaced.

questions.question: How are the competing bulk phases obtained?

options.b: built-in crystallographic prototypes (AFLOW/ICSD parameters) relaxed with the same model, plus --extra files

questions.explanation: e.g. Cr3C2 (D5_10), Cr7C3 (D10_1), Cr23C6 (D8_4), CrF3 (D0_12), NiF2 rutile, Ni3N, β-Mo2C.

questions.question: Hands-on: which bulk phase has the largest CHGNet error vs experiment in the shipped examples?
questions.explanation: It does not enter the Mo2C decomposition, but shows why DFT confirmation matters.

questions.question: Which cell degrees of freedom relax for a 2D sheet?
questions.explanation: relax(..., two_d=True).

questions.question: What does monolayer_from_bulk do?

options.b: finds the van der Waals gaps of a layered crystal, isolates one layer and adds vacuum

questions.explanation: Use with exfoliation_energy for generic 2D materials.

questions.question: Which command asks interactively for the elements and the passivation?
questions.explanation: Arguments given on the command line skip the questions; --no-input never asks.
